results.title: Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1 | Beyond the News
highlights:
# Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1

Fireworks' current pricing table shows September 1 increases across H100, H200, B200, B300 and GB300 on-demand deployments, with B200 rising from $10 to $13 per GPU-hour. Dedicated training jobs that use the same GPU-hour rates inherit the new economics.

Reviewed and published by Lars Jansen Updated 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 4 min read Copy link

 First published 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 

## Key details

1. The new Fireworks on-demand GPU rates begin September 1, 2026.
2. H100 80GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
3. H200 141GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
4. B200 180GB: $10 → $13 per GPU-hour.
5. B300 288GB: $12 → $15 per GPU-hour.
6. GB300 288GB: $18 → $20 per GPU-hour.
7. On-demand deployments are billed per GPU second with no extra startup charges.
8. Region-restricted deployments are priced at a 1.5× premium.
9. Dedicated Training API jobs use the same on-demand GPU-hour pricing.

...

5.

...

## What changed

Fireworks' current pricing page publishes a two-column transition for its on-demand GPU deployments: prices through August 31 and new rates from September 1, 2026. H100 80GB and H200 141GB increase from $7 to $8 per GPU-hour; B200 180GB rises from $10 to $13; B300 288GB from $12 to $15; and GB300 288GB from $18 to $20. Fireworks bills on-demand deployments per GPU second with no startup charge, and its Dedicated Training API uses the same GPU-hour pricing, so the change affects both dedicated serving and GPU-hour training jobs. Region-restricted deployments continue to carry a 1.5× premium.

...

Dedicated GPU economics can dominate the unit cost of high-volume inference, fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning workloads. These increases range from roughly 11% to 30%, large enough to change break-even points between accelerator generations, serverless APIs and competing GPU clouds. The biggest increase is on B200, where a workload consuming 1,000 GPU-hours per month moves from $10,000 to $13,000 before regional premiums or other services. Teams should therefore benchmark completed-task throughput rather than choosing hardware on hourly price or peak specifications alone.

## The September increase varies materially by accelerator

H100 and H200 move from $7 to $8 per hour, about a 14.3% increase. B200 rises 30% from $10 to $13, B300 rises 25% from $12 to $15 and GB300 rises about 11.1% from $18 to $20. The uneven changes can alter the relative cost ranking of GPUs even when performance remains unchanged.

...

Fireworks states that Dedicated Training API jobs are priced per GPU hour using the On-Demand Pricing section. Teams running reinforcement fine-tuning or dedicated training should therefore update both serving and training forecasts, not only inference deployment budgets.

## Per-second billing limits idle waste but not rate exposure

On-demand deployments are billed by the second and do not charge extra startup time, which remains useful for bursty workloads. But sustained fleets still absorb the full hourly increase, and a region-restricted deployment costs 1.5 times the listed rate.

## Hourly price is not total inference cost

A more expensive accelerator can still win if it materially improves throughput, latency or batch efficiency. Builders should compare cost per successful request, training run or completed agent task under the exact model, quantization, context and concurrency they use.

results.title: Cheapest H100 and B200 Cloud: CoreWeave vs Nebius vs Lambda vs Crusoe · Aliteq
results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
On each provider's own pricing page on Nov 3, 2026, Crusoe had the cheapest on-demand H100 ($3.90 a GPU-hour, rising to $4.50 on Dec 1) and Lambda the cheapest B200 ($6.69). CoreWeave was the most expensive on demand, but its fixed spot prices undercut everyone's on-demand rate. The full table, the catches, and where the marketplace tier sits.

...

Which big GPU cloud is cheapest for H100 and B200? On each provider's own pricing page on November 3, 2026: for the H100, Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour on demand, with Lambda a cent behind at $3.99 on an 8-GPU instance. For the B200, Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x), well under Nebius ($8.50) and CoreWeave ($8.60). CoreWeave is the most expensive on demand, but if your job can be interrupted its published spot prices ($2.46 an H100, $4.26 a B200, per GPU) undercut everyone's on-demand rate. Two dates to know: Crusoe's own page says its H100 goes to $4.50 on December 1, 2026, which hands the cheapest on-demand H100 to Lambda.

## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

Among CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe, the cheapest on-demand H100 on November 3, 2026 was Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour, then Lambda at $3.99 (8x instance), Nebius at $4.50 and CoreWeave at $6.16 (an 8-GPU node at $49.24 an hour). Crusoe's page says its H100 rises to $4.50 on December 1, 2026. The cheapest on-demand B200 was Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x; $6.99 on one GPU), then Nebius at $8.50 and CoreWeave at $8.60; Crusoe's B200 is contact-sales. For interruptible work, CoreWeave's spot nodes work out to $2.46 per H100 and $4.26 per B200, and Nebius preemptible starts from $0.79 (H100) and $0.99 (B200) at a dynamic rate. Smaller clouds go lower still: Hyperstack listed a B200 at $6.00 and an H100 at $2.50.

results.title: The Cloud GPU Price War 2026: Neoclouds vs Hyperscalers
highlights:
- Neoclouds list an on-demand H100 from ~$2.89/hr (RunPod) to ~$3.99/hr (Together AI); Nebius lists $3.85/GPU-hr
- Hyperscaler list prices are far higher: AWS p5 works out to ~$6.88/GPU-hr, Azure ND H100 v5 to ~$12.29/GPU-hr (third-party trackers; not confirmed on primary pages)
- One Aug 2026 report puts neocloud rentals up to 66% below the large incumbent clouds
- But contract prices rose: SemiAnalysis' H100 1-year index climbed from ~$1.70 (Oct 2025) toward ~$2.35/GPU-hr (Mar 2026)
- CoreWeave raised list prices ~25% across SKUs in July 2026 and called capacity “effectively sold out”
- AWS quietly raised H200 Capacity Block prices ~15% on Jan 4, 2026 — reportedly its first EC2 GPU price increase in ~two decades
- Nebius disclosed a capacity auction clearing 15% above its highest-ever Blackwell price
- Net: spot/older-Hopper pricing softened; premium, reserved, and Blackwell pricing firmed or rose

AWS — ~15% H200 Capacity Block increase (Jan 4, 2026)

AWS raised prices on its H200 EC2 Capacity Blocks by roughly 15% effective January 4, 2026 — p5e.48xlarge reportedly moved from $34.61 to $39.80/hr — without a formal customer announcement, in what multiple outlets described as its first EC2 GPU price increase in roughly two decades of EC2 pricing (GIGAZINE, Jan 7, 2026). results.title: What It Actually Costs to Rent an H100, H200, or B200 in August 2026
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
- As of early August 2026, on-demand H100 rental runs about $2–4/GPU-hr on specialty clouds (GMI ~$2.00, RunPod ~$1.99–2.69, Lambda ~$3.99) versus a ~$13–14/hr median on AWS/GCP/Azure/Oracle — a 5–7× spread for the identical card.
- H200 lands around $2.60–6.31/hr on-demand (GMI ~$2.60, Lambda ~$5.29, Nebius ~$5.50, CoreWeave ~$6.31); the Blackwell B200 is ~$4.99–6.50/hr (Lambda ~$4.99, Nebius ~$5.50, CoreWeave contract-oriented), with spot dipping near $2/hr where available.
- Prices move weekly and vary by region, commitment, and stock — treat every figure here as a published-rate snapshot, not a quote.
- The decision isn't 'who is cheapest' — it's utilization. On-demand only wins if your GPU is busy; below roughly 40–50% duty cycle, a per-token API almost always beats renting metal.

...

## The price map (published on-demand rates, early August 2026)#

Every figure below is a published on-demand rate, gathered the first week of August 2026 from public pricing trackers. GPU pricing moves weekly with supply, region, and commitment — read this for the shape of the market, then confirm on the provider's own page before you commit a dollar.

- H100 (80GB) — the workhorse. Roughly $1.99–$4/hr on specialty clouds: ~$1.99 at RunPod, ~$2.00 at GMI Cloud, ~$3.99 at Lambda. Spot dips to about $1.20/hr where offered. Hyperscaler median: ~$13.96/hr — the same card, 5–7× the money.
- H200 (141GB) — more memory, bigger models on one card. About $2.60–$6.31/hr on-demand: ~$2.60 at GMI, ~$5.29 at Lambda, ~$5.50 at Nebius, ~$6.31 at CoreWeave. The full cross-provider range runs roughly $2.29 to $13.78/hr.
- B200 (Blackwell) — the frontier card. Published on-demand is ~$4.99/hr at Lambda, ~$5.50/hr at Nebius (SXM6), and roughly $6.50/hr at CoreWeave (whose B200 is largely contract-oriented, not a public on-demand rate). Spot B200 has appeared near $2.12/hr.

highlights:

- CoreWeave's published rates are $6.16 per GPU-hour for HGX H100, $6.31 for H200, $8.60 for B200, and $10.50 for GB200 NVL72, all sold as fixed-size instances with an 8-GPU minimum except NVL72's 4-GPU bundles.

results.title: ISSUE #7: The B300 Trickle
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
Weekly Cloud Pricing Pulse, week ending August 24, 2026: the floor held, and an established chip is still finding its public price 

 Published August 25, 2026 · Pricing evidence through August 24, 2026 · Ornn Compute Price Index (OCPI) through August 23, 2026, 20:00 UTC. 

 The LinkedIn edition of the AIForge Works Weekly Cloud Pricing Pulse: one read on public GPU cloud pricing across nine providers, every week. 

 The one-line read. The four public floors did not move this week: H100 SXM $3.85, H200 $4.29, B200 $6.69, A100 SXM4 $2.30, the same levels we have shown since mid-July. Two things moved around them. The OCPI transaction index rose under three of the four floors, narrowing every gap on the board. And the B300, a chip that has been shipping since last year, is still finding a public price: only a few clouds list it on-demand, intermittently, and where they do the numbers range from about $7.85 to about $26.15 per GPU-hour. A settled floor, a firming index underneath it, and an established Blackwell GPU whose public price is still a trickle. 

## This week 

- Floors held. All four board floors are unchanged: H100 SXM $3.85 (Nebius), H200 $4.29 (Crusoe), B200 $6.69 (Lambda), A100 SXM4 $2.30 (Crusoe), the same levels we have published since mid-July. Across all nine indexed providers, no comparable public on-demand rate moved more than 1% week over week.
- The index moved under them. The floors held, but the OCPI transaction index did not. Week over week it rose for H100 ($2.64 to $2.87), B200 ($5.93 to $6.64), and A100 SXM4 ($1.02 to $1.07), and fell for H200 ($4.75 to $4.42). With the floors flat, every gap on the board narrowed. B200’s floor is now just $0.05 above the index, the tightest spread on the board.
- The B300 trickle. The B300 is an established Blackwell-generation GPU, in market since last year, with prior history in the AIForge Works catalog. What is still catching up is its public price. Only a handful of clouds list it on-demand, and they do so intermittently: AWS’s eight-GPU p6-b300.48xlarge appeared in Seoul for the first time in our reviewed history this week (Linux and four licensed operating-system variants), while Nebius listings dropped and then returned. We now see publicly listed on-demand B300 rates from three providers, AWS, OCI, and Nebius; CoreWeave shows the SKU but its rate is still contact-sales. The listed rates disagree sharply, from about $7.85 per GPU-hour (Nebius, three regions) to about $26.15 (AWS, Seoul). That is catalog visibility, not orderable capacity, and it is what a chip still finding its public price looks like.

...

The four numbers you would take into a renewal did not move, H100 $3.85, H200 $4.29, B200 $6.69, A100 SXM4 $2.30. ... The catalog floor held; the transactional market moved up to meet it. That is a firming market, not a soft one, and it is the kind of thing a single weekly number would miss if it only reported the floor.

...

The public catalog rates AIForge Works presents are on-demand and normalized to a per-GPU-hour basis unless stated otherwise. OCPI is transaction-index context, not a catalog price. Listed or indexed does not mean orderable, and neither is a live quote, an availability guarantee, or a purchase recommendation. Verify current pricing, availability, terms, and fees directly with the provider before acting.
